title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Chemistry (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Chemistry (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not means of checking purity of organic analytes?
questions.explanation: All listed methods are used to check the purity of organic analytes.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a derivative of carboxylic acids?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes and ketones are not derivatives of carboxylic acids.

questions.questionText: The +1 oxidation state is more stable than +3 oxidation state for which group 13 element?
questions.explanation: Thallium (Tl) is the only group 13 element where the +1 oxidation state is more stable than the +3 state due to the inert pair effect, which becomes prominent in heavier elements.

questions.questionText: What is the number of functional groups in acetyl salicylic acid?
questions.explanation: Acetyl salicylic acid contains 2 functional groups.

questions.questionText: Blow air onto your hand with your mouth wide open and then your lips puckered. When does the air look cooler and why? Assume the process is so fast that Q = 0.
questions.explanation: The air feels cooler when puckered due to increased velocity and decreased pressure.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is incorrect?
options: Virtual population analysis estimates the abundance of population in water
Virtual population analysis enables the scientist to predict the future catches
Harvesting a fish population with compromising its future yields is called sustainable yield.
Habitat quality changes affects the population fishes
questions.explanation: Habitat quality changes do affect fish populations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following classified as a conjugate acid base?
questions.explanation: H3O+ and H2O form a conjugate acid-base pair. A conjugate acid-base pair differs by only a proton (H+). H3O+ is the acid that donates a proton to become H2O, which is its conjugate base.

questions.questionText: If limiting molar conductivity of Ca2+ and Cl– are 119.0 and 76.3 S cm² mol⁻¹ respectively, then the value of limiting molar conductivity of CaCl2 will be ____ S cm² mol⁻¹.
questions.explanation: The limiting molar conductivity of CaCl2 = λ⁰(Ca²⁺) + 2 × λ⁰(Cl⁻) = 119.0 + 2 × 76.3 = 119.0 + 152.6 = 271.6 S cm² mol⁻¹. The factor 2 is needed because one CaCl2 produces one Ca²⁺ and two Cl⁻ ions.

questions.questionText: The current is due to concentration gradient of electroactive species in polarography is ------
questions.explanation: The current in polarography is primarily due to diffusion current.

questions.questionText: The property of buffer solution to resist any change in its pH value is known as ------
questions.explanation: Buffer action refers to the ability of a buffer solution to resist changes in pH.

questions.questionText: Of the following electron configurations of neutral atom, which represents an atom in an excited state?
questions.explanation: The configuration 1s²2s²2p⁵3s² represents an excited state because the 2p orbital is not filled completely (should be 2p⁶) before electrons are placed in the 3s orbital, violating the Aufbau principle.

questions.questionText: In TLC, if the compounds are not colored, what technique will be used to visualize?
questions.explanation: Both UV light and iodine vapor methods can be used for visualization.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the principle of Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy?
options: Radiation is absorbed by non-excited atoms in vapor state and are excited to higher states
Medium absorbs radiation and transmitted radiation is measured
questions.explanation: Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy is based on the absorption of radiation by non-excited atoms.

questions.questionText: For the reaction, A + B → C, ΔHo = +30 kJ; ΔSo = +50 J/K. Therefore the reaction is:
options: Spontaneous at temperatures less than 600 K.
Spontaneous at temperatures greater than 600 K.
questions.explanation: Using ΔG = ΔH - TΔS, the reaction becomes spontaneous when TΔS > ΔH. Converting units: ΔSo = +0.050 kJ/K. Solving for T: T > ΔH/ΔS = 30/0.05 = 600 K. Therefore, the reaction becomes spontaneous at temperatures above 600 K.

questions.questionText: In an electrochemical cell, anode and cathode are ___________ respectively.
questions.explanation: In an electrochemical cell, the anode is the negative electrode (where oxidation occurs) and the cathode is the positive electrode (where reduction occurs). Electrons flow from anode to cathode through the external circuit.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is specific properties of dichromate?
options: When acidifying turns to orange color chromate solution
questions.explanation: Dichromate is known as a strong oxidizing agent.

questions.questionText: Lanthanide contraction is caused due to ---------
options: The appreciable shielding on outer electrons by 4f electrons from the nuclear charge
The appreciable shielding on outer electrons by 5d electrons from the nuclear charge
The same effective nuclear charge from Ce to Lu
The imperfect shielding on outer electrons by 4f electrons from the nuclear charge
questions.explanation: Lanthanide contraction is due to the imperfect shielding of 4f electrons.

questions.questionText: Which of the following type of glass is treated to be far more resistant to breakage than simple annealed glass?
questions.explanation: Toughened glass is treated to enhance its resistance to breakage.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not the routine tests carried out on fats and oils?
questions.explanation: Hydrogenation is not a routine test for fats and oils.

questions.questionText: When working in laboratory one of your friend's splash acid on his/ her hands. What first aid treatment did you give for your friends?
options: Washing his/her hands by strong acid for 15 minutes.
Washing his/her hands by plastic bottle water for 2 minutes.
Washing his/her hands by water for 15 minutes.
Washing his/her hands by sodium carbonate solution for 10 minutes.
questions.explanation: The correct first aid treatment is to wash the affected area with water for 15 minutes.

questions.questionText: During working with HPLC, on what nature of the sample components can be depends on?
questions.explanation: HPLC depends on the volatility, miscibility, and polarity of sample components.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not the use of chromatography technique?
options: It is used to separate mixture of compounds
It is used for quantitative determination of mixture of compounds
It is used for identification of components of mixtures
It is used to study the behavior of some chemical reactions
questions.explanation: Chromatography is not typically used to study the behavior of chemical reactions.

questions.questionText: What are the three fundamental theories that govern gravimetric analysis?
options: The law of mass percent, the solubility product and the common ion effect
Law of mass action, principle of solubility product, and the common ion effect
The law of reversible reactions, the solubility product, and the mass action
The law of mass action, reversible reactions and the common ion effect
questions.explanation: Gravimetric analysis is governed by the law of mass action (which describes chemical equilibria), the principle of solubility product (which describes the dissolution equilibrium of sparingly soluble salts), and the common ion effect (which affects solubility when a common ion is added).

questions.questionText: Chromatography is a physical method that is used to separate and analyse _____
questions.explanation: Chromatography is used to separate and analyze complex mixtures.

questions.questionText: All are belongs to extrinsic properties of the substance except.
questions.explanation: Temperature is an intensive property, not an extrinsic property. Extrinsic (extensive) properties depend on the amount of substance, such as volume and mass, while intensive properties like temperature and pressure do not depend on the amount.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the source of light in atomic absorption spectroscopic technique?
questions.explanation: The hollow cathode lamp is commonly used as a light source in atomic absorption spectroscopy.

questions.questionText: (Crystal Field Theory) Strong field ligands such as CN-:
options: Usually produce high spin complexes and small crystal field splitting's.
Usually produce low spin complexes and small crystal field splitting's.
Usually produce low spin complexes and high crystal field splitting's.
Usually produce high spin complexes and high crystal field splitting's.
questions.explanation: Strong field ligands like CN- typically produce low spin complexes with large crystal field splitting.

questions.questionText: The reaction of benzoyl chloride with amines lead to the formation of:
questions.explanation: The reaction of benzoyl chloride with amines produces benzamide.

questions.questionText: In characteristics vibrational energy, absorption frequency depends on -----
options: Masses of atoms in the bonds
questions.explanation: Absorption frequency depends on the masses of atoms, geometry, and bond strength.

questions.questionText: What is the common side product formed along soap during preparation of soap?
questions.explanation: Glycerol is a common byproduct formed during the saponification process.

questions.questionText: During sample analysis in the laboratory, the sample must be ----------
options: Containers must be first filled with inert gas to displace air
Organic components must not be stored in plastic containers
questions.explanation: All listed practices are important for proper sample analysis.

questions.questionText: After liquefaction of the real gases which of the following thermodynamic quantity doesn't change very much?
questions.explanation: The number of moles (D) doesn't change during liquefaction. During this phase transition, pressure and temperature can remain constant while volume changes significantly. The amount of substance (moles) is conserved during physical changes.

questions.questionText: A method by which hydrophobic particles of an ore are separated from hydrophilic particles in a metallurgical pretreatment process is -----
questions.explanation: Flotation is used to separate hydrophobic particles from hydrophilic ones.

questions.questionText: What is the angular momentum quantum number, l, of the electron that is most easily removed when ground state aluminum is ionized?
questions.explanation: Aluminum has the electron configuration [Ne]3s²3p¹. The most easily removed electron is the 3p¹ electron, which has an angular momentum quantum number l = 1.

questions.questionText: Which of the following lists the forms of coal from lowest to highest concentration of carbon?
questions.explanation: The correct order from lowest to highest carbon concentration is lignite, bituminous, anthracite.

questions.questionText: In a galvanic cell, the electrons flow from:
options: Anode to cathode through the external circuit
Cathode to anode through the solution
Anode to cathode through the solution
Cathode to anode through the external circuit
questions.explanation: In a galvanic cell, electrons flow from the anode to the cathode through the external circuit. The anode is where oxidation occurs (loss of electrons), while reduction occurs at the cathode (gain of electrons).

questions.questionText: Which of the following method is not means of purifying contaminated or mixture of organic compounds?
questions.explanation: Spectroscopic analysis is not a purification method.

questions.questionText: The oils and fats are extracted from a variety of __________
questions.explanation: Oils and fats can be extracted from fruits, seeds, and nuts.

questions.questionText: What are the units of k for the rate law: Rate = k[A][B]², when the concentration unit is mol/L?
questions.explanation: For the rate law Rate = k[A][B]², the overall order is 3 (1 from [A] and 2 from [B]²). Since units for concentration are mol/L, the units for k are L² mol⁻² s⁻¹ to make the overall units for rate mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹.

questions.questionText: Which one of following statements about nitrogen balance is correct?
options: Nitrogen balance is the ratio of intake of nitrogenous compounds / output of nitrogenous metabolites from the body
In nitrogen equilibrium the excretion of nitrogenous metabolites is greater than the dietary intake of nitrogenous compounds.
Positive nitrogen balance means that there is a net loss of protein from the body
In positive nitrogen balance the excretion of nitrogenous metabolites is less than the dietary intake of nitrogenous compounds.
questions.explanation: In positive nitrogen balance, the body retains more nitrogen than it excretes.

questions.questionText: The speed of migration of ions in electric field depends upon ----
options: Magnitude of charge and shape of molecule
Magnitude of charge shape and mass of molecule
Magnitude of charge and mass of molecule
questions.explanation: The speed of migration depends on the charge, shape, and mass of the ions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following conditions and reaction mechanism matched wrongly?
options: Methyl or primary alkyl halides, SN2 predominantly
Powerful nucleophiles, especially those with negative charges, SN1 mechanism
questions.explanation: Option D is incorrectly matched. Powerful nucleophiles, especially those with negative charges, favor the SN2 mechanism, not SN1. The SN1 mechanism is favored by weak nucleophiles and proceeds via a carbocation intermediate regardless of nucleophile strength.

questions.questionText: If a salt bridge is removed between the half cells in electrochemical cell, the voltage is ------ ?
questions.explanation: Removing the salt bridge disrupts the circuit, causing the voltage to drop to zero.

questions.questionText: Which methods is the most rapid and most effective for the isolation of individual lanthanide elements from the mixture?
questions.explanation: Ion exchange chromatography is the most rapid and effective method for separating individual lanthanide elements. This technique utilizes the slight differences in the binding affinity of lanthanide ions to ion exchange resins, allowing for their separation despite their very similar chemical properties.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is wrong regarding dyes?
questions.explanation: Dyes must be conjugated, not non-conjugated. The extended conjugation in dyes allows them to absorb visible light, which gives them their color. Options B, C, and D are all correct characteristics of dyes.

questions.questionText: Which one is an example of polar aprotic solvent?
questions.explanation: Acetone is a polar aprotic solvent.

questions.questionText: Which of the following sampling term is incorrectly defined?
options: Laboratory sample – smaller, homogeneous sample taken from the bulk and has the same composition as the bulk
Lot – the total material from which samples are taken
Aliquot – small portions of the bulk sample taken for individual analysis
Sample preparation – the series of steps that convert a representative bulk sample into a form suitable for analysis
questions.explanation: The definition of laboratory sample is incorrect. A laboratory sample may not always have exactly the same composition as the bulk due to sampling errors and heterogeneity of the bulk material. It aims to be representative but perfect homogeneity is often not achievable.

questions.questionText: The colored complexes of the transition elements have color because they ------
options: Absorb light of some visible wavelengths
Absorb light of some ultraviolet wavelengths
questions.explanation: Transition metal complexes have color because they absorb specific wavelengths within the visible spectrum. The color we observe is the complementary color to the wavelength that is absorbed. This absorption occurs due to d-d electronic transitions that fall within the energy range of visible light.

questions.questionText: What is the overall order of the reaction for the following data: [A]0 [B]0 Initial D[C]/Dt 0.100 M 0.100 M 4.00 × 10⁻⁵ mol/L • s 0.200 M 0.100 M 8.00 × 10⁻⁵ mol/L • s 0.100 M 0.200 M 1.60 × 10⁻⁴ mol/L • s?
questions.explanation: The overall order of the reaction is 2.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of utilizing the basic oxygen furnace after the blast furnace in the production of iron?
options: To convert pig iron to steel
To convert pig iron to cast iron
To convert cast iron to pure iron
To remelt, run into molds, and cool pig iron
questions.explanation: The basic oxygen furnace is used to convert pig iron into steel.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a common oxidizing agent?
questions.explanation: KMnO4 is a common oxidizing agent.

questions.questionText: Which of the following set of chemical elements is classified as the secondary macronutrients of plants?
questions.explanation: Sulfur, magnesium, and calcium are classified as secondary macronutrients.

questions.questionText: If HCl adds to an unsymmetrical alkene like propene, there are two possible ways it could add. However, in practice, there is only one major product. What is this major product?
questions.explanation: The major product is 2-chloropropane due to Markovnikov's rule.

questions.questionText: In quantum mechanics light sometimes appears to behave as —
questions.explanation: Light exhibits both wave-like and particle-like properties.

questions.questionText: Which of the following organic compound is not symmetrical?
questions.explanation: 2-butanol is not symmetrical due to its chiral center.

questions.questionText: As of the Basic Components of Spectroscopic Instrumentation; which one is used to measure the intensity of the Electromagnetic radiation that falls on it?
questions.explanation: The detector measures the intensity of electromagnetic radiation.

questions.questionText: If Carnot engine operating between two heat reservoirs at 227 ºC and 27 ºC absorbs 1000 calories from the 227 ºC reservoir per cycle, how much heat is discharged into the 27 ºC of reservoir?
questions.explanation: For a Carnot engine, efficiency = 1 - (T_cold/T_hot). Converting to Kelvin: T_hot = 500K, T_cold = 300K. Efficiency = 1 - (300/500) = 0.4 or 40%. With 1000 cal input, work done = 0.4 × 1000 = 400 cal. Heat discharged = Input heat - Work = 1000 - 400 = 600 cal.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a type of non-probability sampling?
questions.explanation: Stratified random sampling is a type of probability sampling.

questions.questionText: A 1.00 mole sample of ammonia at 14.0 atm and 25°C in a cylinder fitted with a movable piston expands against a constant external pressure of 1.0 atm. At equilibrium, the pressure and the volume of the gas are 1.0 atm and 23.5 liters respectively. The final temperature of the sample is? Use R=0.08206 L atm/K mol.
questions.explanation: Using the ideal gas law, PV = nRT. Rearranging for T: T = PV/nR = (1.0 atm × 23.5 L)/(1.00 mol × 0.08206 L atm/K mol) = 286 K. The gas cools during expansion against a lower external pressure.

questions.questionText: In which type of chromatography, the stationary phase held in a narrow tube and the mobile phase is forced through it under pressure?
questions.explanation: Column chromatography involves forcing the mobile phase through a stationary phase in a narrow tube.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about Physical property of vanadium?
options: Vanadium is hard, steel grey and bright white metal.
In massive state vanadium is not attacked by air, water, alkalis or non-oxidizing acids.
questions.explanation: All statements about the physical properties of vanadium are correct.

questions.questionText: A device that converts the solution into fine spray or droplets is called -------
questions.explanation: An atomizer is used to convert liquid into a fine spray.

questions.questionText: For which order reaction is the half-life of the reaction independent of the initial concentration?
questions.explanation: In zero-order reactions, the half-life is independent of the initial concentration.

questions.questionText: A cylinder contains 7.0 g of nitrogen gas. How much work must be done to compress the gas at constant temperature of 80°C until the volume is halved?
questions.explanation: The work done can be calculated using the ideal gas law and the work formula for isothermal processes.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is properties based polymer name?
questions.explanation: Natural is a properties-based classification of polymers, referring to polymers that occur in nature like cellulose, starch, proteins, etc. Strong is a characteristic but not a classification category. Monomer refers to the building blocks, and copolymer describes a polymer made from multiple monomer types.

questions.questionText: The root mean square speed of the molecules of a gas is 1260 m/s. The most probable speed of the molecules is ------
questions.explanation: The relationship between root mean square speed (vrms) and most probable speed (vmp) is: vmp = (√2/√3) × vrms. Substituting: vmp = (√2/√3) × 1260 m/s = (1.414/1.732) × 1260 = 0.816 × 1260 = 1028.8 m/s.

questions.questionText: Ordinary soap is ---------------
questions.explanation: Ordinary soap is a salt of carboxylic acids.

questions.questionText: A zero order reaction is 40% complete at the end of 20 min. What is the value of the rate constant?
questions.explanation: The rate constant can be calculated based on the zero-order kinetics.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a biomolecule?
questions.explanation: H2SO4 is an inorganic compound and not a biomolecule.

questions.questionText: Which compound is zero-valent metal complex?
questions.explanation: [Ni(CO)4] is a zero-valent metal complex.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct?
options: The magnetic properties of [Fe(CN)6]⁴⁻ is higher than [Fe(H2O)6]²⁺
The magnetic properties of [Fe(CN)6]⁴⁻ is lower than [Fe(H2O)6]²⁺
[Fe(CN)6]⁴⁻ is high spin complex whereas [Fe(H2O)6]²⁺ is low spin complex
All of the above are correct.
questions.explanation: [Fe(CN)6]⁴⁻ is a low-spin complex due to the strong-field CN⁻ ligands, while [Fe(H2O)6]²⁺ is a high-spin complex due to the weak-field H₂O ligands. This means [Fe(CN)6]⁴⁻ has fewer unpaired electrons and thus lower magnetic properties than [Fe(H2O)6]²⁺. Option D is incorrect because option C has the spin states reversed.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following methods is the most suitable for amino-acid analysis?
questions.explanation: Ion exchange chromatography is commonly used for amino acid analysis.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a correct interpretation of the results of Rutherford's experiments in which gold atoms were bombarded with alpha particles?
options: Electrons in atoms are arranged in shells.
Neutrons are the center of an atom.
Neutrons and protons in atoms have nearly equal mass.
The positive charge of an atom is concentrated in a small region.
questions.explanation: Rutherford's experiments showed that the positive charge is concentrated in a small nucleus.

questions.questionText: Which of the following separation techniques is dependent on the difference in volatility?
questions.explanation: Distillation separates components based on their volatility.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of oxidation reaction?
options: The conversion of nitrobenzene into aniline
The conversion of acetaldehyde into acetic acid
The conversion of cyclohexanone into cyclohexane
questions.explanation: The conversion of acetaldehyde into acetic acid is an oxidation reaction.

questions.questionText: Ion exchange chromatography is based on ------ ?
questions.explanation: Ion exchange chromatography relies on electrostatic attraction between ions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a chiral molecule?
questions.explanation: 2-butanol is chiral due to its asymmetric carbon atom.

questions.questionText: The small portion of electromagnetic radiation that the human eye responds to is ---
questions.explanation: The visible spectrum is the range of light that the human eye can detect.

questions.questionText: What is the ΔE for the formation of 3 moles of CO at 1.0 atm and 25 °C if the standard enthalpy of formation of carbon monoxide is -110.5 kJ/mole and R is 0.0821 L atm/K mol?
questions.explanation: For 3 moles of CO: ΔH = 3 × (-110.5 kJ) = -331.5 kJ. For gases, ΔE = ΔH - ΔnRT. Here, Δn = 0 for the reaction C(s) + ½O₂(g) → CO(g) (assuming this is the formation reaction), so ΔE = ΔH = -331.5 kJ.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a petroleum product?
questions.explanation: All listed options are petroleum products.

questions.questionText: An industry requires pure water for many applications and uses a variety of purification techniques, which source of water is expected to contain the greatest alkalinity range?
questions.explanation: Groundwater typically has a greater range of alkalinity due to mineral content.

questions.questionText: During working with HPLC, on what nature of the sample components can it depend?
questions.explanation: HPLC depends on the volatility, miscibility, and polarity of sample components.

questions.questionText: The component of interest in the sample is called ________.
questions.explanation: The component of interest is referred to as the analyte.

questions.questionText: What is the number of functional groups in acetyl salicylic acid?
questions.explanation: Acetyl salicylic acid contains 2 functional groups.

questions.questionText: The method of analysis involves determining the conversion into a compound having some specific properties by which an element or ion is known as:
questions.explanation: This describes chemical methods of analysis.

questions.questionText: What is the molality of ethanol in a solution of total volume 100 ml prepared by adding 50 ml ethanol (density = 0.789 g/ml) to 50 ml water (density = 1.0 g/ml)?
questions.explanation: Molality = moles of solute / kg of solvent. Mass of ethanol = 50 ml × 0.789 g/ml = 39.45 g. Moles of ethanol = 39.45 g / 46.07 g/mol = 0.857 mol. Mass of water = 50 ml × 1.0 g/ml = 50 g = 0.05 kg. Molality = 0.857 mol / 0.05 kg = 17.14 mol/kg, which rounds to option A (17 mol/kg).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a major cause of environmental degradation?
questions.explanation: Improper waste disposal is a significant cause of environmental degradation.

questions.questionText: Lactones are:
questions.explanation: Lactones are defined as cyclic esters.
